The closure below calls self.child_widget (&mut self) and never reads self.order, so the take is safe and avoids the per-layout clone (the clone exists only to dodge the borrow, §19).

Stop collecting a fresh Vec<f32> per layout. Keep a scratch field `gaps: Vec<f32>` on the sliver: inside the existing borrow block do `self.gaps.clear(); self.gaps.extend(range.clone().map(|position| drag.gap_offset(position)));`, then `let gaps = std::mem::take(&mut self.gaps);` before the children map (child_widget needs &mut self) and `self.gaps = gaps;` after it. Hoisting and clear() per §2/§11.

Each widgets entry does a linear scan of self.order every layout, which is O(widgets x items) per frame. Use the inverse index (see the set_child_extent finding) so the check is O(1): `self.widgets.retain(|item, _| self.position_of(*item).is_some());`, or keep a small `Vec<bool>` / bitset of live items rebuilt when order changes.

Linear search per measured child makes layout O(n^2). Maintain an inverse index `position_of: Vec<usize>` (item id to visual position) updated wherever `order` is written (the reorder completion and the `self.order = next_order` assignment), then `self.position_of.get(item).copied()` here.

Runs on structural changes, not every frame, but the retain is O(keys x entries) with a Vec allocation. Build a set once and test membership in O(1): `let live: std::collections::HashSet<u64> = next.iter().map(|entry| entry.id).collect();` then `self.base_extents.retain(|id, _| live.contains(id));`, and the same for `self.widgets.retain(...)`.
